_comment: All static prose for the HTML report. Edit freely — no Python changes needed; just re-run `python3 carcache.py report`.
HTML is allowed in any string (, , , …).
$placeholders are substituted with live values from profile.json / the data, so the text can never drift from the actual scoring.
Unknown placeholders are left as-is rather than crashing, and any key you delete falls back to a built-in default.
Available placeholders are listed per block in the sibling `_placeholders` entries.
title: Car Analyzer: final report
intro: Data-driven scoring model to assist with selection of exact car model based on matching mobile.de listings.

header.sub: Updated on $date · $n_ranked cars ranked · $n_live currently live

ranking.heading: Ranking
ranking.sub: Summary table with cars ordered by the weighted total score

methodology.heading: Methodology
methodology.sub: Details on how each score is calculated · Per-car breakdown for each criteria is below

criteria_matrix.heading: Scores matrix
criteria_matrix.sub: Raw scores on scale 0–10 per criterion

reliability.heading: Reliability
reliability.sub: Computed from objective independent figures matched to each listing based on TÜV - the model’s Mängelquote for the car’s age band and ADAC - its breakdowns-per-1000 for the car’s registration year (both lower = better). Each value is mapped to 0–10 scale vs a fixed market reference (s), then averaged 50/50. Older band / year ⇒ higher rate ⇒ lower score. ADAC values are official (Pannenstatistik 2025); TÜV values are modelled from the official age-band averages (per-model print table); “–” = no value (scored on the other metric), n/a = neither (fallback).

safety.heading: Safety (Euro NCAP) — informational, not scored
safety.sub: Every model here is 5-star, and NCAP percentages are not comparable across test years — the protocol gets stricter every few years, so 85% under the 2018 protocol is not worse than 94% under the 2012 one. Scoring this would rank test vintage, not safety; it is shown for reading, with the test year, and deliberately kept out of the ranking.

condition.heading: Condition
condition.sub: Every listing starts at 10 and loses points for what the seller discloses. This scores the disclosure, not an inspection: a seller who reports a fault is penalised while a silent one is not, and “accident-free not stated” is a paperwork gap rather than evidence of damage.

equipment.heading: Equipment
equipment.sub: Scores how many of wishlist items each listing carries (✓) · The Equipment score blends this weighted wishlist ($eq_wishlist_pct) with registration-year recency ($eq_year_pct, the year column) — newer kit is newer-generation even with the same boxes ticked

stability.heading: How stable is this ranking?
stability.sub: Influence = weight × spread of scores — what each criterion actually contributes to the order. A criterion every car scores the same on cannot rank anyone, whatever its weight; compare share to the nominal weight when tuning. Below it, the same ranking recomputed hundreds of times with randomly perturbed weights: if the winner keeps winning, the decision does not hinge on the exact weights.

power.heading: Power
power.sub: A proxy for relaxed high-speed cruising, built from engine power plus a bonus for a mid-size estate or a big engine · All parts are added then clamped to 0–10

cost.heading: Cost of ownership
cost.sub: The composite money score, and the annual running cost underneath it
cost.composite_sub: Asking price ($cost_price_pct) · price rating ($cost_rating_pct) · cash running cost ($cost_running_pct). Each → its own 0–10, then the weighted mean. Depreciation is shown in the bars below but not scored: it is derived from the asking price, which already has its own third. ● marks a car whose fuel cost uses measured real-world consumption (spritmonitor.de) instead of the listing's WLTP figure — hover for the litres and sample size. WLTP here runs 2–44% optimistic depending on the engine, so it is not a constant that cancels out.
cost.tco_sub: ADAC-style, $tco_hold_years-yr hold at $tco_annual_km km/yr · Bar width ∝ €/yr · Hover a segment for its value · The Cost score uses the cash part (everything except depreciation)

notes.heading: Notes & findings
notes.sub: What an LLM read out of each seller's own description, with the quote it relied on. Severity is stated by the reviewer, not guessed from keywords: major and minor feed the Condition score, notes never do.

_placeholders_methodology: reliability: $rel_midpoint $rel_gain $rel_metric_weights $rel_tuv_mean $rel_tuv_sd $rel_adac_mean $rel_adac_sd $rel_fallback · condition: $pen_accident $pen_acc_unknown $pen_owner $pen_no_service $pen_no_tuv $pen_major $pen_minor $pen_minor_cap · equipment: $eq_wishlist_pct $eq_year_pct $eq_year_worst $eq_year_best $eq_wishlist_list · power: $ab_base $ab_per_ps $ab_segment_bonuses $ab_big_bonus $ab_big_cm3 · cost: $cost_price_best $cost_price_worst $cost_price_pct $cost_rating_pct $cost_running_pct $cost_running_best $cost_running_worst $cost_rating_scale $cost_rating_unknown $tco_hold_years $tco_annual_km $tco_fuel_price $phev_share_pct $phev_kwh $phev_price_kwh $phev_petrol · mileage: $ml_best_km $ml_worst_km · location: $loc_origin $loc_best $loc_worst $loc_fallback

reliability.body: Two objective figures, matched to this exact listing: the TÜV Mängelquote for the car’s age band and the ADAC breakdowns per 1000 for its registration year (both lower = better). Each is mapped to 0–10 against a fixed market reference, then averaged 50/50. Older band/year ⇒ higher rate ⇒ lower score.
reliability.details: s = clamp($rel_midpoint + $rel_gain·(mean − cell)/sd, 0, 10) per metric, then weighted $rel_metric_weights. Reference (frozen, so ranking a subset never re-scales): TÜV mean $rel_tuv_mean / sd $rel_tuv_sd; ADAC mean $rel_adac_mean / sd $rel_adac_sd. ADAC cells are the official ADAC Pannenstatistik 2025 per-year values; TÜV cells are modelled from the official age-band averages (the per-model table is print-only). A model with no cell for one metric is scored on the other; with neither it gets the neutral fallback $rel_fallback and an n/a badge.

condition.body: Starts at 10 and subtracts what the seller discloses: accident status, extra owners, missing service history or TÜV, and defects mentioned in the listing notes.
condition.details: Deductions: accident confirmed −$pen_accident, accident-free not stated −$pen_acc_unknown, −$pen_owner per owner beyond the first, no service history −$pen_no_service, no TÜV −$pen_no_tuv, −$pen_major per disclosed major defect (leak, head gasket, rust-through, engine/gearbox damage), −$pen_minor per minor caution capped at −$pen_minor_cap. Clamped to 0–10. Caveat: this scores disclosure, not an inspection — a seller who honestly reports a fault is penalised while a silent one is not, and “accident-free not stated” is a paperwork gap, not evidence of damage. Defect severities come stated from the LLM findings (see Notes & findings), never guessed from keywords; an accident is charged exactly once — the declaration when the seller ticked it, the finding only when the tick-box says accident-free but the text admits damage.

equipment_fit.body: $eq_wishlist_pct weighted share of the wishlist actually fitted, plus $eq_year_pct registration-year recency — a deliberate preference: a newer car's kit is newer-generation (infotainment, ADAS revisions) even with identical boxes ticked, so age is allowed to count here as well as in Reliability.
equipment_fit.details: Wishlist: $eq_wishlist_list. Towbar counts only when fitted, not merely “capable”. Year maps linearly $eq_year_worst → 0 … $eq_year_best → 10, clamped. Options every candidate has (CarPlay, heated seats, cruise) are deliberately excluded — they are part of the search filter, so scoring them would shift every car by a constant instead of separating them.

autobahn.body: From engine power: a base of $ab_base plus $ab_per_ps per PS above 130, plus a bonus for a mid-size estate or a big engine. A proxy for relaxed high-speed cruising.
autobahn.details: clamp($ab_base + $ab_per_ps·max(0, PS−130) + bonus, 0, 10). Bonus = the best of the segment match ($ab_segment_bonuses) or +$ab_big_bonus for ≥ $ab_big_cm3 cm³. A per-model entry in autobahn.map overrides the formula outright.

cost.body: One composite money score from three things a single €/yr figure cannot separate: what you pay (asking price), whether that price is fair (mobile.de's own verdict for this exact car), and what it costs to keep (the annual cash running cost). A cheap car can still be poor value; a well-priced car can still be expensive to run. Each contributes $cost_price_pct / $cost_rating_pct / $cost_running_pct.
cost.details: Asking price — absolute curve, €$cost_price_best → 10, €$cost_price_worst → 0, linear and clamped. Price rating — mobile.de's five buckets mapped to $cost_rating_scale; an unrated listing scores $cost_rating_unknown (neutral), since silence is not a bad price. Running cost (cash) — petrol, electricity, maintenance, insurance, road tax and HU per year, on its own absolute curve: €$cost_running_best → 10, €$cost_running_worst → 0. Depreciation is displayed but not scored: it is estimated from the asking price, which already has its own third — scoring it too would charge the same euros twice. All three parts are absolute, so a car's Cost score never moves when you rank a subset. ADAC Autokosten structure over a $tco_hold_years-year hold at $tco_annual_km km/yr at €$tco_fuel_price/l. Kfz-Steuer is computed exactly (§8 KraftStG); maintenance and insurance are estimates anchored to ADAC reference figures. Plug-in hybrids: the WLTP l/100km is a blended figure that assumes charging and ignores the electricity you buy, so it is discarded — instead $phev_share_pct of the km run on grid power ($phev_kwh kWh/100km at €$phev_price_kwh/kWh) and the rest on the engine at $phev_petrol l/100km. Full/mild hybrids are untouched.

mileage.body: Absolute odometer curve: $ml_best_km km → 10, $ml_worst_km km → 0, linear and clamped.
mileage.details: Deliberately absolute rather than relative to the other candidates, so a car’s mileage score never changes just because you ranked a different subset — and a field of similar cars gets similar scores instead of being stretched across the whole range.

location.body: Absolute travel-time curve from $loc_origin to the dealer: ≤ $loc_best min → 10, ≥ $loc_worst min → 0. At $loc_best min, Berlin and effectively all of Brandenburg score 10.
location.details: Travel time is fetched once per listing (carcache.py travel: Nominatim geocode + OSRM driving route) and stored on the record, so ranking never touches the network. Preference order is public transport → car time → car distance → straight-line; public transport is currently unavailable (the free DB endpoint returns 503), so listings carry real driving times. Unknown ⇒ fallback $loc_fallback. The weight is deliberately small: visiting the car is a one-time trip, not a cost of ownership — and this criterion's wide spread means it punches above its nominal weight (see the stability section).
